title: Server-Side Request Forgery and Cloud Metadata Access Static Analysis Rules

rules.name: Outbound request to a dynamically built URL
rules.description: An outbound HTTP client call (requests, httpx, urllib.request, aiohttp) receives a URL assembled with an f-string, '+' concatenation, '%' formatting, str.format() or a bare variable. When that value comes from request data the server fetches an attacker-chosen destination, reaching internal services, cloud metadata endpoints or localhost-only admin interfaces.
rules.remediation_example: host = urlparse(candidate).hostname; if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS: raise ValueError('blocked'); requests.get(candidate, timeout=5)

rules.name: Cloud metadata endpoint hardcoded in an outbound request
rules.description: An outbound HTTP client call targets a cloud instance metadata service (169.254.169.254 or metadata.google.internal). Reaching this endpoint hands the caller the instance role credentials, so code that fetches it on demand turns any URL-fetching feature into full cloud credential theft.
rules.remediation_example: Use the provider SDK credential chain (boto3 default session, google.auth.default()) instead of fetching the metadata endpoint directly.
